question: What type of pollutants does the WHO Ambient Air Quality Database monitor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** maintains the **Ambient Air Quality Database**, which serves as a critical global tool for tracking **ground-based measurements** of air pollution levels in urban and rural settlements.
 
• The primary pollutants monitored in this database are **particulate matter** with a diameter of **10 microns** or less (**PM₁₀**) and **2.5 microns** or less (**PM₂.₅**).
 
• In the latest **2022 update** of the database, the scope was expanded to include over **6,000 cities** and settlements across **117 countries**, making it the most comprehensive record of air quality to date.
 
• The database is instrumental in monitoring **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 11.6.2**, which specifically measures the **annual mean levels** of fine particulate matter in cities to ensure sustainable urban living.
